source_text: Ἢ τάχα διὰ τὸ ἀκαριαῖον καὶ ἄχρονον τῆς δημιουργίας εἴρηται τὸ, Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν, ἐπειδὴ ἀμερές τι καὶ ἀδιάστατον ἡ ἀρχή. Ὡς γὰρ ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς ὁδοῦ οὔπω ὁδὸς, καὶ ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς οἰκίας οὐκ οἰκία, οὕτω καὶ ἡ τοῦ χρόνου ἀρχὴ οὔπω χρόνος, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ μέρος αὐτοῦ τὸ ἐλάχιστον. Εἰ δὲ φιλονεικῶν τις χρόνον εἶναι λέγοι τὴν ἀρχὴν, γινωσκέτω ὅτι διαιρήσει αὐτὴν εἰς τὰ τοῦ χρόνου μέρη. Ταῦτα δέ ἐστιν, ἀρχὴ, καὶ μέσα, καὶ τελευτή. Ἀρχὴν δὲ ἀρχῆς ἐπινοεῖν παντελῶς καταγέλαστον. Καὶ ὁ διχοτομῶν τὴν ἀρχὴν, δύο ποιήσει ἀντὶ μιᾶς, μᾶλλον δὲ πολλὰς καὶ ἀπείρους, τοῦ διαιρεθέντος ἀεὶ εἰς ἕτερα τεμνομένου. Ἵνα τοίνυν διδαχθῶμεν ὁμοῦ τῇ βουλήσει τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀχρόνως συνυφεστάναι τὸν κόσμον, εἴρηται τὸ, Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν. Ὅπερ ἕτεροι τῶν ἑρμηνευτῶν, σαφέστερον τὸν νοῦν ἐκδιδόντες, εἰρήκασιν, Ἐν κεφαλαίῳ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς, τουτέστιν, ἀθρόως καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ. Τὰ μὲν οὖν περὶ ἀρχῆς, ὡς ὀλίγα ἀπὸ πολλῶν εἰπεῖν, ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον. 1.7 Ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ τῶν τεχνῶν αἱ μὲν ποιητικαὶ λέγονται, αἱ δὲ πρακτικαὶ, αἱ δὲ θεωρητικαί· καὶ τῶν μὲν θεωρητικῶν τέλος ἐστὶν ἡ κατὰ νοῦν ἐνέργεια· τῶν δὲ πρακτικῶν, αὐτὴ ἡ τοῦ σώματος κίνησις, ἧς παυσαμένης οὐδὲν ὑπέστη οὐδὲ παρέμεινε τοῖς ὁρῶσιν· ὀρχήσεως γὰρ καὶ αὐλητικῆς τέλος οὐδὲν, ἀλλ' αὐτὴ εἰς ἑαυτὴν ἡ ἐνέργεια καταλήγει· ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ποιητικῶν τεχνῶν, καὶ παυσαμένων τῆς ἐνεργείας, προκείμενόν ἐστι τὸ ἔργον· ὡς οἰκοδομικῆς καὶ τεκτονικῆς καὶ χαλκευτικῆς καὶ ὑφαντικῆς, καὶ ὅσαι τοιαῦται, αἳ, κἂν μὴ παρῇ ὁ τεχνίτης, ἱκανῶς ἐν ἑαυταῖς τοὺς τεχνικοὺς λόγους ἐμφαίνουσι, καὶ ἔξεστί σοι θαυμάσαι τὸν οἰκοδόμον ἀπὸ τοῦ ἔργου, καὶ τὸν χαλκέα καὶ τὸν ὑφάντην. Ἵνα οὖν δειχθῇ ὅτι ὁ κόσμος τεχνικόν ἐστι κατασκεύασμα, προκεί μενον πᾶσιν εἰς θεωρίαν, ὥστε δι' αὐτοῦ τὴν τοῦ ποιήσαντος αὐτὸν σοφίαν ἐπιγινώσκεσθαι, οὐκ ἄλλῃ τινὶ φωνῇ ἐχρήσατο ὁ σοφὸς Μωϋσῆς περὶ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ' εἶπεν, Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίη σεν· οὐχὶ ἐνήργησεν, οὐδὲ ὑπέστησεν, ἀλλὰ Ἐποίησεν. Καὶ καθότι πολλοὶ τῶν φαντασθέντων συνυπάρχειν ἐξ ἀϊδίου τῷ Θεῷ τὸν κόσμον, οὐχὶ γεγενῆσθαι παρ' αὐτοῦ συνεχώρησαν, ἀλλ' οἱονεὶ ἀποσκίασμα τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ ὄντα αὐτομάτως παρυποστῆναι· καὶ αἴτιον μὲν αὐτοῦ ὁμολογοῦσι τὸν Θεὸν, αἴτιον δὲ ἀπροαιρέτως, ὡς τῆς σκιᾶς τὸ σῶμα, καὶ τῆς λαμπηδόνος τὸ ἀπαυγάζον· τὴν οὖν τοιαύτην ἀπάτην ἐπανορθούμενος ὁ προφήτης, τῇ ἀκριβείᾳ ταύτῃ τῶν ῥημάτων ἐχρήσατο εἰπὼν, Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός. Οὐχὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὴν αἰτίαν τοῦ εἶναι παρέσχεν, ἀλλ' ἐποίησεν ὡς ἀγαθὸς τὸ χρήσιμον, ὡς σοφὸς, τὸ κάλλιστον, ὡς δυνατὸς, τὸ μέγιστον. Μόνον γὰρ οὐχὶ τεχνίτην σοι ἔδειξεν ἐμβεβηκότα τῇ οὐσίᾳ τῶν ὅλων, καὶ τὰ καθ' ἕκαστον μέρη πρὸς ἄλληλα συναρμόζοντα, καὶ τὸ πᾶν ὁμόλογον ἑαυτῷ καὶ σύμφωνον καὶ ἐναρμονίως ἔχον ἀποτελοῦντα. Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἐκ δύο τῶν ἄκρων τοῦ παντὸς τὴν ὕπαρξιν παρῃνίξατο, τῷ μὲν οὐρανῷ τὰ πρεσβεῖα τῆς γενέσεως ἀποδοὺς, τὴν δὲ γῆν δευτερεύειν φάμενος τῇ ὑπάρξει.
thought_title: The beginning is not a part of time, and 'made' shows God as craftsman
orientation: Basil is expounding the first words of Genesis, 'In the beginning God made,' and has just begun his first homily on the six days of creation.
pass_a_gloss: Or perhaps because of the instantaneous and timeless character of the creation it was said, 'In the beginning he made,' since the beginning is something without parts and without extension. For just as the beginning of a road is not yet a road, and the beginning of a house is not a house, so also the beginning of time is not yet time, nor even the smallest part of it. But if someone, being contentious, says that the beginning is time, let him know that he will divide it into the parts of time. And these are beginning, and middle parts, and end. But to conceive of a beginning of a beginning is altogether ridiculous. And the one who cuts the beginning in two will make two instead of one, or rather many and infinite ones, since what is divided is always cut into further parts. In order therefore that we might be taught that the world came into existence together with the will of God timelessly, it was said, 'In the beginning he made.' Which other interpreters, rendering the sense more clearly, have said, 'In summary God made,' that is, all at once and in a short time. The matters concerning the beginning, then, to speak a few things from many, are sufficient up to this point. 1.7 And since of the arts some are called productive, and others practical, and others theoretical; and of the theoretical arts the end is the activity according to the mind; and of the practical arts, the end is the movement itself of the body, and when this ceases nothing has come into being nor remained for those who see; for of dancing and flute-playing there is no end product, but the activity itself terminates in itself; but in the case of the productive arts, even when the activity has ceased, the work is set forth; as of house-building and carpentry and bronze-working and weaving, and as many as are of this sort, which, even if the craftsman is not present, sufficiently display in themselves the technical principles, and it is possible for you to admire the house-builder from the work, and the bronze-worker and the weaver. In order therefore that it might be shown that the world is a technical construction, set forth for all for contemplation, so that through it the wisdom of the one who made it might be recognized, the wise Moses used no other word about it, but said, 'In the beginning he made'; not 'he worked,' nor 'he brought into existence,' but 'He made.' And inasmuch as many of those who imagined that the world coexists with God from eternity did not grant that it came into being from him, but that, being as it were a shadow of his power, it came into existence automatically; and they confess God as its cause, but as a cause without deliberate choice, as the body is the cause of the shadow, and the shining thing is the cause of the radiance; correcting therefore such deception, the prophet used this precision of words, saying, 'In the beginning God made.' He did not merely provide this very cause of its being, but he made as good the useful thing, as wise the most beautiful thing, as powerful the greatest thing. For he all but showed you a craftsman entering into the substance of all things, and fitting the individual parts to one another, and producing the whole harmonious with itself and concordant and having itself in tune. In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. From the two extremes of the universe he indicated the existence, giving to the heaven the prerogative of generation, and saying that the earth holds second place in existence.

choices.why: Basil reports this as a clearer rendering by other interpreters of 'in the beginning,' meaning all at once; 'summary' captures the sense of a comprehensive act rather than a temporal point.
rejected: In a chief point God made

choices.english: all at once and in a short time
choices.why: Basil glosses 'in summary' with these two adverbial phrases; 'all at once' conveys simultaneity and 'in a short time' conveys brevity, matching the contrast with a temporal beginning.
Basil uses this phrase to argue the world is a crafted artifact that reveals its maker; 'technical construction' preserves the artisanal force of τεχνικόν and the made-object sense of κατασκεύασμα.

choices.term: οὐχὶ ἐνήργησεν, οὐδὲ ὑπέστησεν, ἀλλὰ Ἐποίησεν
choices.english: not 'he worked,' nor 'he brought into existence,' but 'He made'
choices.why: Basil contrasts three verbs to insist on deliberate making; 'he worked' for ἐνήργησεν and 'he brought into existence' for ὑπέστησεν keep the distinction from the chosen 'made' (ἐποίησεν).
rejected: not 'he operated,' nor 'he established,' but 'He created'

choices.why: This is the view Basil rejects; 'shadow' renders ἀποσκίασμα literally and preserves the image of automatic, unchosen emanation.

choices.english: but as a cause without deliberate choice
choices.why: Basil distinguishes between God as cause and God as deliberate maker; 'without deliberate choice' renders ἀπροαιρέτως precisely, contrasting with the willed act of making.
rejected: but as a cause not by preference

bible_refs.note: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν

pass_b_english: Or perhaps the words “In the beginning God made” were chosen because the act of creation was instantaneous and outside time, since a beginning is something without parts and without extension. Just as the beginning of a road is not yet a road, and the beginning of a house is not a house, so the beginning of time is not yet time—not even the smallest part of it. And if someone argues contentiously that the beginning is time, let him understand that he will be dividing it into the parts of time: beginning, middle, and end. But to imagine a beginning of a beginning is utterly laughable. The person who cuts the beginning in two will make two beginnings instead of one—or rather many, even infinite, since whatever is divided is always cut into further pieces. So to teach us that the world came into existence together with the will of God, outside time, Scripture says, “In the beginning God made.” Other translators, expressing the meaning more clearly, have said, “In summary God made”—that is, all at once and concisely. Let this much suffice, then, as a brief account drawn from many possible remarks about the beginning.

Now among the arts, some are called productive, others practical, and others theoretical. The end of the theoretical arts is the activity of the mind. The end of the practical arts is the movement of the body itself, and when that movement stops, nothing remains or persists for those who see it; for dancing and flute-playing have no end product, but the activity itself terminates in itself. In the productive arts, however, even when the activity has ceased, the work remains before us—as with house-building, carpentry, metalworking, weaving, and all such crafts. Even if the craftsman is not present, these works sufficiently display the skill of their makers in themselves, and you can admire the builder from his building, the metalworker and the weaver from their work. So to show that the world is a technical construction, set before all for contemplation, so that through it the wisdom of its Maker might be known, the wise Moses used no other word about it. He said, “In the beginning God made”—not “he worked,” nor “he brought into existence,” but “He made.” And since many people have imagined that the world coexisted with God from eternity and was not made by him, but rather came into existence automatically as a kind of shadow of his power—they acknowledge God as its cause, but as a cause without deliberate choice, like a body causing its shadow or a light causing its radiance—the prophet corrects this error by using the precise wording, “In the beginning God made.” God did not merely supply the cause of its being; as good, he made what is useful; as wise, what is most beautiful; as powerful, what is greatest. He has all but shown you a craftsman entering into the substance of all things, fitting each individual part to the others, and producing a whole that is consistent with itself, harmonious, and perfectly ordered. “In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth.” By the two extremes of the universe he indicated its existence obliquely, giving the heaven the first place in origin and saying that the earth holds second place in existence.

problems.quote: all at once and in a short time
problems.why: ἐν ὀλίγῳ means 'in brief'/'concisely' (of expression), not 'in a short time' (of duration)
problems.ruling: ἐν ὀλίγῳ here parallels ἀθρόως ('all at once'); context is creation's brevity, not concise expression.

problems.quote: as good, for its usefulness; as wise, for its beauty; as powerful, for its greatness
problems.source_quote: ὡς ἀγαθὸς τὸ χρ�σιμον, ὡς σοφὸς τὸ κάλλιστον, ὡς δυνατὸς τὸ μέγιστον
problems.why: Misreads syntax: τὸ χρήσιμον etc. are objects made, not purposes; 'as good, he made what is useful'
problems.fix: as good, he made what is useful; as wise, what is most beautiful; as powerful, what is greatest
problems.ruling: ὡς ἀγαθὸς τὸ χρήσιμον = 'as good, the useful thing'; objects not purposes. English misreads syntax.

he made it as good, for its usefulness; as wise, for its beauty; as powerful, for its greatness
edits.new: as good, he made what is useful; as wise, what is most beautiful; as powerful, what is greatest

fixed: ἀθρόως καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ: ἐν ὀλίγῳ means 'in brief'/'concisely', not 'in a short time'; changed to 'all at once and concisely'.

ὡς ἀγαθὸς τὸ χρήσιμον, ὡς σοφὸς τὸ κάλλιστον, ὡς δυνατὸς τὸ μέγιστον: the adjectives are objects made, not purposes; changed to 'as good, he made what is useful; as wise, what is most beautiful; as powerful, what is greatest'.

last_rejected.why: ἀκαριαῖον means instantaneous/momentary, not just outside time; both aspects lost
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκαριαῖον (instantaneous) is captured by 'instantaneous' earlier in same sentence; ἄχρονον as 'outside time' is accurate.

last_rejected.quote: the activity itself terminates in itself
last_rejected.source_quote: αὐτὴ εἰς ἑαυτὴν ἡ ἐνέργεια καταλήγει
last_rejected.why: καταλήγει means ends/comes to an end, not terminates; 'terminates' is too final/absolute
last_rejected.fix: the activity itself ends in itself
last_rejected.ruling: καταλήγει means 'ends/terminates'; 'terminates in itself' is within normal range for the philosophical sense.

last_rejected.why: τεχνικόν means crafted/skillful, not 'technical' in modern sense; loses artisanal meaning
last_rejected.ruling: 'Technical' derives from τέχνη and is standard for τεχνικόν; context clarifies artisanal meaning, not modern machinery.

last_rejected.why: ὑπέστησεν means caused to subsist/established, not 'brought into existence'; distinct from creation
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπέστησεν means 'brought into existence'; the contrast with ἐποίησεν is preserved in context.

last_rejected.why: παρυποστῆναι means subsided alongside/emerged alongside, not 'came into existence'; specific philosophical term
last_rejected.ruling: παρυποστῆναι with αὐτομάτως means 'came into existence alongside'; 'came into existence' captures the core meaning adequately.

last_rejected.quote: as a cause without deliberate choice
last_rejected.why: ἀπροαιρέτως means without deliberate purpose/will, not merely 'without deliberate choice'; stronger negation of agency
last_rejected.fix: as a cause without purpose or will
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπροαιρέτως means 'without deliberate choice/purpose'; 'without deliberate choice' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: God did not merely supply the cause of its being
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐχὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὴν αἰτίαν τοῦ εἶναι παρέσχεν
last_rejected.why: αὐτὸ τοῦτο means 'this very thing' or 'merely this'; English weakens the contrast with deliberate making
last_rejected.fix: God did not merely provide the cause of its being
last_rejected.ruling: 'Merely' captures αὐτὸ τοῦτο ('this very thing' = only this); contrast with deliberate making is preserved.

last_rejected.why: ἐμβεβηκότα means having stepped into/embarked upon, with sense of active engagement; 'entering' too weak
last_rejected.ruling: ἐμβεβηκότα means 'entered/stepped into'; 'entering' is standard and adequate for the metaphor.

last_rejected.why: παρῃνίξατο means hinted at obscurely/riddlingly, not 'indicated obliquely'; stronger sense of enigmatic hint
last_rejected.ruling: παρῃνίξατο means 'indicated obliquely/hinted'; 'indicated obliquely' is within normal range of meaning.
